title: Grade 4 Math — Wed, May 27
description: Perimeter & Area — Day 3 of 5: Perimeter vs Area — when to use which
subject: mathematics

questions.question: You want to put a fence around a garden. Do you need perimeter or area?
options: Perimeter — total length around the edge
questions.explanation: Fence goes around the outside → you need the perimeter (total edge length).

questions.question: You want to tile a floor. Do you need perimeter or area?
questions.explanation: Tiles cover the inside surface → you need the area.

questions.question: Rectangle: 9 cm × 4 cm. Find both perimeter AND area.
Two rectangles: A is 6×4 cm, B is 8×3 cm. Which has a larger area?
questions.explanation: A = 6×4 = 24 cm². B = 8×3 = 24 cm². Same area, different shapes!

questions.question: Same two rectangles (6×4 and 8×3). Which has a larger perimeter?
questions.explanation: P of A = 2×(6+4) = 20 cm. P of B = 2×(8+3) = 22 cm. B has bigger perimeter!

questions.question: A shape has perimeter 16 cm. If it's a square, what is its area?
Grass seed for a lawn 15 m × 8 m: seed for area or perimeter?
questions.explanation: Grass seed covers the whole lawn surface → Area = 15×8 = 120 m².

questions.question: Border tiles around a 10 m × 6 m pool. Do you use perimeter or area?
questions.explanation: Border tiles go around the edge → Perimeter = 2×(10+6) = 32 m.

questions.question: Square field has area 100 m². What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Area = side² → 100 = side² → side = 10 m. Perimeter = 4×10 = 40 m.

questions.question: Can two shapes have the same perimeter but different areas?
options: No — same perimeter always means same area
Yes — a square and rectangle can have same perimeter but different areas
Only if they are the same shape
No — perimeter and area are always proportional
questions.explanation: Yes! Example: Square 5×5 (P=20, A=25) and rectangle 8×2 (P=20, A=16). Same P, different A.

questions.question: Frame (border) for a painting 40 cm × 30 cm. Length of frame needed?
questions.explanation: Frame goes around edge = perimeter = 2×(40+30) = 140 cm.

questions.question: A rectangle has area 60 m² and perimeter 34 m. Find length and width.
A garden 20 m × 15 m: fencing costs ₹30/m, turf costs ₹15/m². Which total cost is more?
L-shaped room: 8×5 m with a 3×2 m section removed. What is the area?
questions.explanation: Large rectangle area = 8×5 = 40 m². Removed section = 3×2 = 6 m². L-shape area = 40−6 = 34 m².

questions.question: Book cover is 25 cm × 18 cm. Another book is 30 cm × 15 cm. Which cover has more area?
questions.explanation: First: 25×18 = 450 cm². Second: 30×15 = 450 cm². Same area!
